title: Lapsing a Caveat
text:
• Proof of service of the Notice to Caveator to Take Proceedings on Caveat (this must be served on the caveator using 
one of the acceptable service methods referred to below) 
• Proof that the person causing the notice to be served has an interest in the land, mortgage or encumbrance that the 
caveat relates to 

Important dates to remember 
• You cannot file the lapse at the Land Titles office until the 60-day notice period has expired (may be shorter if ordered 
by the court). 
• When calculating the expiry date, the 60-day time period does not include the day the notice was served. 
• If a CLP has been filed within the 60-day time period, the caveat cannot be lapsed. 
 
Acceptable methods of service 
• There are multiple service methods depending on whether the caveator is an individual or a corporate caveator. For 
all options, please refer to the procedure’s manual referenced below. 
Other information 
o The 60-day time period may be shortened by a court order. 
 
Additional Information 
Detailed information regarding land titles filing requirements and forms can be found on our website: 
• Main webpage 
o https://www.alberta.ca/land-titles.aspx 
 
• Caveat policy
